abstract.t: A profile of RFC 8032 for nish/crypto/ed25519: PureEdDSA Ed25519 key generation, signing and verification. Every requirement quotes RFC 8032, the main source; every binding sentence of RFC 8032 (MUST, MUST NOT, SHALL, SHALL NOT, REQUIRED) is tested or excluded here.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

nish/crypto/ed25519 implements Ed25519 as RFC 8032 Section 5.1 defines it, with an empty context and no prehash. The private key is the 32-octet seed, which the module takes as a Secret. Key generation and signing return u8[] | null, null for a seed of the wrong length; verification returns a boolean.

section.name: Interface
section.sourcecode: // module: nish/crypto/ed25519 export const ed25519PublicKey = (seed: Secret<u8[]>): u8[] | null export const ed25519Sign = (seed: Secret<u8[]>, msg: u8[]): u8[] | null export const ed25519Verify = (pub: u8[], msg: u8[], sig: u8[]): boolean

section.name: Ed25519

blockquote.t: For Ed25519, dom2(f,c) is the empty string.
The context (if present at all) MUST be empty.

section.t: Untested: nish implements PureEdDSA Ed25519 only: no function takes a context, so it is always empty

blockquote.t: The 32-byte public key is generated by the following steps.
The public key A is the encoding of the point [s]B.
Form the signature of the concatenation of R (32 octets) and the little-endian encoding of S (32 octets; the three most significant bits of the final octet are always zero).
If any of the decodings fail (including S being out of range), the signature is invalid.

section.name: Security Considerations

blockquote.t: In particular, unless the underlying protocol does not require it, the receiver MUST buffer the entire message (or enough information to reconstruct it, e.g., compressed or encrypted version) to be verified.

section.t: Untested: an obligation on the caller: ed25519Verify takes the whole message, and what the receiver does with it is outside the module

section.name: Out of Scope
section.t: Ed25519ctx and Ed25519ph (RFC 8032 Section 5.1) and Ed448 and Ed448ph (Section 5.2) are not exported, so their sections and their test vectors (Sections 7.2 to 7.5) are not part of this profile.
Three statements of RFC 8032 are not functional and hold no BCP 14 keyword, so they are recorded here, not excluded:

li.t: Section 5.1.5: the private key is "cryptographically secure random data". The seed is the caller's input, and its randomness is not observable by a test.

Section 8.1: "the modulo p arithmetic must not use any data-dependent branches". Timing is not observable by a functional test. nish checks the field arithmetic Ed25519 shares with X25519 on the emitted machine code (tests/cases/ct_asm_x25519.ts) and records the rest in docs/security/crypto-ecc.md (ECC-5).

Section 8.1: "secrecy of the private key is fundamental". nish takes the seed as a Secret and pins the wipes of its hash, the nonce and the scratch under opt -O2 (tests/wipes/crypto.js, tests/run.js), recorded in docs/security/crypto-ecc.md.

section.t: Of Section 7.1, only the public keys are vectors:

li.t: Signatures: vector extract refuses every signing row. Under the label the section prints, such as "MESSAGE (length 1 byte)", the argument is "not a literal", since a Call label admits only letters, digits, - and spaces. Under "MESSAGE", fidelity refuses it because the value is printed under "MESSAGE (length 1 byte)". TEST 1's empty message is printed only as a length, and fidelity wants "" or "(0 octets)". TEST 1024's 1023-byte message fits as hex pairs; only its label blocks it.
Verification: a row expecting true must cover a requirement cited to Section 7.1 that states the result, and the section states none.

section.t: The properties hold signing and verification instead, and tests/link/crypto_ed25519/rfc.ts signs and verifies all five Section 7.1 tests against the printed signatures.
std/crypto/ed25519.ts also exports three i32 constants, which a vector or property cannot call:

li.t: ED25519_SEED_SIZE: the 32-octet seed every property draws.

section.t: vector 0.2.1 cannot declare outOfScope exports, so this section is their record.

section.name: Properties
section.sourcecode: // P-TAMPER-MSG covers R-VERIFY-EQ — flipping any one bit of the message makes the signature invalid forall (seed: u8[] /* 32..32 */, msg: u8[] /* 1..100 */, bit: i32 /* 0..799 */) => ed25519Verify(unwrap(ed25519PublicKey(seed)), flipBit(msg, bit), unwrap(ed25519Sign(seed, msg))) === false where bit < 8 * msg.length

tr.td: RFC 8032 7.1 TEST SHA(abc): the public key

abstract.t: This document describes elliptic curve signature scheme Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA). The algorithm is instantiated with recommended parameters for the edwards25519 and edwards448 curves. An example implementation and test vectors are provided.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
